author: derekchiang
content:
not sure if you saw the discussion between <@273808422753796097> and <@1126229231572094976> a few days ago on the 8141 signal chat, but they raised a point that for an account to use leanPCS for authentication, the account contract would need to run PIOP over the PCS claims, but since the PCS claims depend on the sighash, if we run the PIOP in a VERIFY frame (whose calldata is committed to sighash), we have a circular dependency PIOP -> PCS claims -> sighash -> PIOP.  if we run PIOP in a proof frame along with the PCS openings, we lose the benefit of aggregation

so it seems that we'd need either 1) a type of PROOF frame whose calldata is readable from VERIFY frames, or 2) we go back to the siglist design with the ARBITRARY bytes which are readable in VERIFY frames

i personally prefer the siglist approach just because again the proof data is more like dependencies whose ordering doesn't matter.  and to enable L2s to permissionlessly deploy new schemes, maybe we could just replace the siglist scheme ID with verifier address instead?

author: niard.eth
content:
<@725415098331430932> impact of the parameters on the signature https://ethresear.ch/t/sphincs-minus-efficient-stateless-post-quantum-signature-verification-on-the-evm/25165 

As you can see there is a lot we can do to offload to the signer without losing the lifetime or security level. The one missing piece in that article is pruning which was presented later by conduition https://conduition.io/cryptography/hypertree-pruning/ and basically replaced the "JARDIN" follow up which was a weird smart contract system to have fast signing. 


Solving the privacy problem in pruning courtesy of our Emile : 

Pruning
Use a single, large, XMSS layer. Weak devices only construct a subtree of 2ᵇ leaves, and use pseudorandom nodes for the rest, and signing grinds until its index lands in it (An idea from conduition). Verifier algo is unaffected.

The risk of reusing a seed under different pruning parameters is fixed by deriving a second seed as H(seed ‖ parameters).

Privacy: one can select the leaf indexes of the non-pruned FTS at (pseudo)random, but signing a lot will always eventually leak the pruning size. Partial remediation: keep a semi-trusted state S of the previously signed FTS, and when grinding lands on a FTS of S, accept it only with probability (2ᵇ − |S|) / (2ʰ − |S|), so that FTS repeat exactly as often as with a full tree. This essentially gives 2ᵇ⁻¹ signatures with no privacy leak. The state is semi-trusted, because an adversary controlling it can: leak the pruning size, and reduce the lifetime by a factor of 2, but nothing worse.
